chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Chick Webb's death and the Baltimore tribute
summary: Soon after returning he played with Ella Fitzgerald's band, which took over after Chick Webb died, at the Baltimore stadium tribute.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Yes, I did go to Baltimore.
Chick died, yeah. They had a tribute to him.
He had died.... Tommy was in the Army...

Yeah, Chick Webb died, and the Ink Spots and Ella took the band over; she was the leader of the band. So they asked me to come and play with the band. Tommy Pulford, I think he was inducted into the Army as I remember, or he might have been ill -- I forget exactly. But I imagine he was inducted. So I went to Baltimore with the band, and we played the tribute for Chick.
This was soon after you got back.
How long did you stay with them?

I don't remember exactly. Not quite a year. I have to just get my thoughts together. We went down there and we did our thing to pay tribute. It was a great, big thing, because Chick was from Baltimore. It was a big stadium, and all the acts were there. Oh, everybody came over to play. Billie Holiday. The City of Baltimore gave their respect to Chick Webb, who happens to be one of their citizens.

So we did that, we were there, and we came back to the Savoy. Like, Ella was the head of the band and Taft was like the overseer of the band. I think from then on, we played several places around; I just can't remember now.
